chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Al-Mustahil, from Muhammad ibn Hanzala, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you, a hadith that I heard from some of your Shia and your Mawalis, reporting it from your father.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is it?'
I said: 'They claimed that he (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The most fortunate state for a man is what we are upon, when the soul is in this (world).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

When that is the case, the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him) comes to him, and Ali (peace be upon him) comes to him, and Jibraeel (peace be upon him) comes to him, and the Angel of Death (peace be upon him) comes to him.
So that Angel says to Ali (peace be upon him): 'O Ali! Indeed, so-and-so was a follower (Mawali) of you and of your Ahl al-Bayt.'
He (peace be upon him) says: 'Yes, he used to have affinity with us and disavow our enemies.'
So the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him) says that to Jibraeel, and Jibraeel raises that report to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.مُوَالِياً: Follower or one who has affinity
key_terms.يَتَوَلَّانَا: He used to have affinity with us

ai.seo_question: What happens to the soul of a Shia follower at the moment of death according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia doctrine of *Mawt al-Sidq* (the truth of death), where the dying believer is visited by a celestial hierarchy: the Prophet Muhammad, Imam Ali, Jibraeel, and Malak al-Mawt. The Angel of Death specifically confirms the deceased's *Wilayah* (loyalty) to the Ahl al-Bayt, which is then elevated by Jibraeel to Allah, emphasizing that allegiance to the Imams is a decisive factor in the spiritual state at the moment of death. This scene underscores the intercessory and witnessing roles of the Imams in the transition from this world to the next.
